messages.text: Will a power spike fry the whole miner?

Great question — this is actually one of the Rev 6.1's standout design choices.

**The onboard F1 fuse takes the hit, not your miner.**

- There's a small automotive-style blade fuse — the **F1 fuse** — mounted right on the board, next to the yellow XT30 power input.
- If a power spike comes through, **F1 blows first**, sacrificing itself to protect the electronics behind it.
- Cheaper miners often omit this entirely — a spike there cooks the whole board.

**The result:** worst case, you replace a ~$0.50 fuse, not a $249 miner.

The included **350 W MEANWELL PSU** also helps — it's a quality industrial supply, not a cheap brick prone to sending dirty power downstream.
Is the included power supply actually reliable?

Yes — and it's genuinely over-engineered for this job.

**MEANWELL LRS-350-12 (350 W / 29 A, UL/CE/UKCA certified)**

- The miner draws **~100 W at full speed** — this PSU is rated for 350 W, so it's **loafing at roughly 30% load** all day, every day.
- Supplies running cool and light like that run for years; it's the stressed-to-the-limit cheap bricks that fail — and when they fail, they can take the miner with them.
- UL/CE/UKCA certified — proper safety testing, not a no-name brick.

**It's also overclock-ready out of the box** — if you ever want to push past 6 TH/s, the headroom is already there, no extra parts needed.

It ships in the box. Unbox → plug in → mine. ⚡
